diagnostics.message: When VPC subnets are configured, :resource.aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper must wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ami_housekeeper_vpc_execution_role. Referencing the execution role ARN does not wait for AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole to be attached, so Lambda creation can race the attachment and fail because the role lacks EC2 network-interface permissions. Add depends_on on the attachment resource; the reverse destroy ordering also keeps these permissions attached during function deletion.

:resource.aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper references the role but does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.ami_housekeeper to install its application permissions. The enabled scheduled target can therefore invoke the function while the AMI housekeeping policy is still being installed, causing authorization failures. Order the function after this inline policy so its existing downstream trigger also waits for the policy.

When tracing is configured, :resource.aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.ami_housekeeper_xray. Its role reference orders only role creation, so the scheduled target can invoke the function before its X-Ray permissions are installed, losing initial traces. Add depends_on on the counted policy resource to order tracing permissions before the function and its downstream trigger.

:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.ami_housekeeper can activate the enabled schedule before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging is installed, allowing invocations before logging is ready. Make the target depend on this policy, which already waits for the managed log group. Do not add that dependency to the Lambda function itself: the policy depends on the log group, which currently depends on the function, so that would introduce a cycle.

:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.ami_housekeeper and :resource.aws_lambda_permission.ami_housekeeper currently share prerequisites but can be created concurrently. The target can begin delivering scheduled events before the permission allows events.amazonaws.com to invoke the function. Make the target depend on the permission so invocation authorization is installed first and retained until the target is removed during destruction.
